### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c6ffa6f9e3c262a305a64af680af5ba377fd16b5` — the merge of head `6148308b535aa0c8401ff786c68fcdeba81c1b8f` into base `fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c6ffa6f9e3c262a305a64af680af5ba377fd16b5 && git checkout c6ffa6f9e3c262a305a64af680af5ba377fd16b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450 6148308b535aa0c8401ff786c68fcdeba81c1b8f && git checkout -B drift-repro fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450 && git merge --no-ff 6148308b535aa0c8401ff786c68fcdeba81c1b8f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6148308b535aa0c8401ff786c68fcdeba81c1b8f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts + packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts, .changeset/33695-system-column-implicit-indexes.md

### ① Derived judgments

- The face is the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration only. Nothing is under `packages/spec/src/**` and no path is governed (`check-governed-merges` = NOT governed), so the owed tier is `TIER_DEFAULT`.
- The widening is one name added to `@objectstack/driver-sql`'s `.` export, `implicitReferenceIndexes`. The function already existed in `schema-drift.ts` (#31882). The diff exports it and adds one optional argument, `physicalColumns?: ReadonlySet<string>`. Its argument and return types (`DeclaredIndexInput`, `ExpectedIndex`) were already exported from the same entry (index.ts L147, L156), so the emitted `.d.ts` names no unexported type.
- With `physicalColumns` absent, the function returns what it did before for every input. The new key filter applies only when the argument is given, so existing callers are unchanged. No exported name is removed or renamed, and no accepted value is refused.
- The only new consumer is `@objectstack/driver-turso`'s remote face (`remote-transport.ts`), a first-party sibling that now reads the composition driver-sql owns instead of duplicating it.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on both packages is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no author-writable key, value or metadata type moves. AGENTS.md step 3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`. No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed for a widening.
- The changeset's widening sentence matches the diff: export name, entry and argument semantics.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The PR adds no id materialisation or in-app join where SQL can push down. The change is DDL composition (index plans), not a read path.
- Behaviour beyond the export (two implicit indexes built by sync, the remote face building the full implicit set) is the card's ordinary scope. It is judged in the ordinary ACCEPT read, not on this face.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay `pr_create`), so no off-relay login to name.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A4-33695`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jUg7BKfRBcTPyMxbLh`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `6148308b535aa0c8401ff786c68fcdeba81c1b8f`
Area: S2 · Fixes #33695 · ordinary ACCEPT read per review-checklist.md. The only contract face is the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration. Its `TIER_DEFAULT` record is the area's own, 6898739480 (PASS), and I read it.

1. **Premise measured, by an M0 bench at 1M rows.**
   - PostgreSQL 16, admin default page statement: 317.0 → 1.33 ms. The plan goes from Parallel Seq Scan plus top-N heapsort to `Index Scan Backward using idx_bench_line_item_created_at_id`.
   - SQLite: the plan is unchanged while the controlled-by-parent chain is present, and goes to `USING INDEX` (1578 → 0.16 ms) without it. That is why landing waits on, or rides with, #33897 (#33696), as the card's "SQLite: land with or after the R4 card" says.
   - Ablations A1–A5 each turn a named pin red and were restored from HEAD.
2. **Mechanism, read on the tree.**
   - `IMPLICIT_SYSTEM_COLUMN_KEYS` adds `(created_at, id)` and `(owner_id)` after the #31882 reference loop.
   - `carriesImplicitSystemKey` admits a builtin column always, admits any other column only as a stored, single-valued field, and never admits the tenant column.
   - A declared index whose key STARTS WITH the whole system key serves instead, so a declared `(created_at)` alone does not count.
   - `physicalColumns` keeps an adopted table without `created_at` free of an unbuildable index and of the `error` line.
   - The rotation gate now opens on the implicit set, so an object with nothing else to index still gets `(created_at, id)` and the sync matches the differ.
   - Turso's remote `buildDeclaredIndexDDL` now appends the same composition, which also closes the #31882 reference-index gap on `libsql://`.
3. **Ruling followed.** 「两个都加」 on #33695 names exactly these two keys. The docblock records that it supersedes #31882 scope B for these two keys only.
4. **Clause-② yes (widening), `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`: right.**
   - The widening is `implicitReferenceIndexes` newly exported from the driver-sql root, plus an optional `physicalColumns`. A new root export is a widening, as in precedents #32848 and #31929.
   - AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 says a non-protocol widening ships `patch`.
   - The changeset names the widening.
   - Dogfood is n/a because the PR has no `!` and no narrowing arm.
5. **Tests.**
   - The new `sql-driver-33695-system-column-indexes.test.ts` has 13 tests and its live PostgreSQL cells ran.
   - The new `turso-33695-implicit-index-parity.test.ts` covers the local/remote parity and an empty remote plan.
   - Eight existing pins now enumerate the new index, and each update is the new row only.
6. **Changeset.** Each sentence matches the diff, including CONCURRENTLY on an existing PostgreSQL table and "a second sync makes no changes".
7. **Accepted deviations (Acceptance notes), with no follow-up owed here:**
   - The write cost was NOT MEASURED. The ruling took on the cost.
   - The tenancy shape: on many-tenant tables, `(organization_id, created_at, id)` would serve better, but the ruling names `(created_at, id)`.
   - The owner index is chosen by selectivity, as the card itself expects.
   - The name `implicitReferenceIndexes` is kept.
8. **Nit.** The rotation gate now calls `columnInfo` and `syncTableIndexes` for every managed table on every boot, where before it skipped tables with nothing to index. That is one more catalog read per table, and its boot cost is not measured. It is an accepted deviation unless the seat wants a reading.
9. **Check-runs on the head:** 36 success, 18 skipped. The one `cancelled` run is a superseded `PR-body guards` run; the same check's latest run on this head is `success`. Nothing has failed or is pending.

The patch-id is `0d57a89c2edfd361c79679b325bc550880f1f780`. A clean main merge that keeps it keeps this PASS. Arm only once #33897 has landed, or with it.
